body.statement: Can \(\mathscr H_{\mathrm{idx}}\) be completed into a finite, non-tautological necessary-and-sufficient criterion, stated only in the covariance-whitened endpoint-face normals, face incidence, and supports of face-complete least-favorable priors, that decides whether a game in \(\mathcal G_p\) lies in \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{all}}\), \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{co}}\), or \(\mathsf C_{\mathrm{none}}\)? The criterion must separately certify ridge factorization of every forced Bayes response and the presence or absence of non-ridge perturbations preserving all binding risks.
body.justification: This exposes the non-tautological geometric classification as the central open content rather than confusing an exhibited index rule with factorization of all optima.
body.gap: MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision proves multiplicity and excludes some threshold rules, while Yata2025Optimal exhibits one optimal index under symmetry; neither classifies the unrestricted optimal correspondence.
body.consumer: A policy maker can learn whether reporting one scalar score is lossless, merely one admissible representation, or impossible for every minimax rule.
